subject: MATH
title: Math 5
description: Fifth-grade mathematics following the CA CCSS sequence: place value through thousandths, fluency with the multi-digit multiplication algorithm, division with two-digit divisors, all four operations with decimals, and the big shift to adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing fractions. Students also build volume concepts, convert measurement units, graph on the coordinate plane, and classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy. Lessons move from concrete models (place value disks, area models, fraction strips, unit cubes) to written strategies and real-world problem solving.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.5.OA.A.1: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions and evaluate expressions with these symbols.
standards.5.OA.A.2: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.
standards.5.OA.B.3: Generate two numerical patterns from two given rules, identify relationships between corresponding terms, and graph the ordered pairs.
standards.5.NBT.A.1: Recognize that a digit in one place represents 10 times what it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents to its left.
standards.5.NBT.A.2: Explain patterns in the number of zeros and decimal point placement when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10; use whole-number exponents for powers of 10.
standards.5.NBT.A.3: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
standards.5.NBT.A.4: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.
standards.5.NBT.B.5: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
standards.5.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients of up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors using place value strategies, properties, and models.
standards.5.NBT.B.7: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths using models, place value strategies, and properties; explain the reasoning.
standards.5.NF.A.1: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing them with equivalent fractions.
standards.5.NF.A.2: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions; use benchmark fractions and number sense to check reasonableness.
standards.5.NF.B.3: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator and solve word problems with quotients that are fractions or mixed numbers.
standards.5.NF.B.4: Apply and extend understanding of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction, including area of rectangles with fractional side lengths.
standards.5.NF.B.5: Interpret multiplication as scaling (resizing) by comparing the size of a product to the size of one factor.
standards.5.NF.B.6: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers.
standards.5.NF.B.7: Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions, and solve related word problems.
standards.5.MD.A.1: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a system and use conversions in multi-step real-world problems.
standards.5.MD.B.2: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit and use fraction operations to solve problems from it.
standards.5.MD.C.3: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures measured in unit cubes.
standards.5.MD.C.4: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and improvised units.
standards.5.MD.C.5: Relate volume to multiplication and addition; apply V = l x w x h and V = B x h, and find volumes of figures composed of two right rectangular prisms.
standards.5.G.A.1: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines (axes) to define a coordinate system and understand ordered pairs.
standards.5.G.A.2: Represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant and interpret coordinate values in context.
standards.5.G.B.3: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories of that category.
standards.5.G.B.4: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

units.title: Place Value and Decimal Fractions
units.big_idea: Our base-ten system extends to the right of the decimal point; each place is 10 times the place to its right.

units.title: Multi-Digit Whole Number Multiplication and Division
units.big_idea: Place value and the properties of operations make efficient algorithms for multiplying and dividing large numbers.

units.title: Decimal Operations
units.big_idea: The same place value reasoning used for whole numbers works for adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing decimals.

units.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
units.big_idea: Fractions can only be combined when they refer to same-sized parts, so we rename them with common denominators.

units.title: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
units.big_idea: A fraction is a division, and multiplying by a fraction scales a quantity up or down.

units.title: Volume
units.big_idea: Volume measures how many unit cubes fill a solid, and it can be found by multiplying layers.

units.title: Measurement Conversions
units.big_idea: Units within a system are related by multiplication, so converting means multiplying or dividing.

units.title: Coordinate Plane and Numerical Patterns
units.big_idea: Ordered pairs locate points on a plane and let us see relationships between two patterns.

units.title: Classifying Two-Dimensional Figures
units.big_idea: Shapes belong to families; a square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram and a quadrilateral all at once.

units.title: Year Review and Capstone
units.big_idea: Fifth-grade math tools combine to solve real, multi-step problems.

weeks.topic: Place value relationships to millions and thousandths
objectives: Explain that each place is 10 times the place to its right
Explain that each place is 1/10 of the place to its left
materials: place value disks or paper squares

days.title: Place value chart
days.work: Build a place value chart from millions to thousandths and write 10 numbers dictated aloud into it, naming the value of each underlined digit.

days.title: Ten times as much
days.work: Use place value disks to show 0.4 becoming 4 and 40 when multiplied by 10; record 8 'times 10' statements with a diagram showing digits shifting left.

days.title: One tenth of
days.work: Model dividing 300, 30 and 3 by 10 with disks (trading for smaller units); write 8 '1/10 of' statements such as 0.07 is 1/10 of 0.7.

days.title: Comparing digit values
days.work: In numbers like 555.555, compare the value of each 5 to its neighbors and solve 10 'how many times greater' problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a 12-question quiz on place value relationships and write one sentence explaining why the decimal point never moves (digits do).

weeks.assessment: Friday quiz: 12 items on place value of whole numbers and decimals plus a written explanation of the 10x relationship.

objectives: Multiply and divide whole numbers and decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000
Write powers of 10 using exponents

days.title: Multiply by powers of 10
days.work: Solve 20 problems like 3.42 x 100 on a place value chart, then describe the pattern of how many places digits shift.

days.title: Divide by powers of 10
days.work: Solve 20 problems like 45 / 1,000 = 0.045 and explain why zeros must be added as placeholders.

days.title: Exponents
days.work: Write 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 as 10^1 through 10^4; expand numbers like 6 x 10^3 and solve 15 mixed exponent problems.

days.title: Metric connection
days.work: Measure 5 household objects in centimeters and convert to meters and millimeters by multiplying or dividing by powers of 10.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 15-problem quiz with powers of 10 and exponents and correct any errors using the place value chart.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on multiplying/dividing by powers of 10 and exponent notation; check of the metric measuring table.

weeks.topic: Reading, writing and comparing decimals to thousandths
objectives: Read and write decimals in standard, word and expanded form
Compare decimals using >, = and <

days.title: Three forms
days.work: Convert 12 decimals among standard form, word form (three and fifty-two thousandths) and expanded form including fraction form like 3 x 1 + 5 x (1/100).

days.title: Modeling thousandths
days.work: Shade 1,000-square grids to show 0.4, 0.40 and 0.400 and explain in writing why these are equivalent.

days.title: Comparing decimals
days.work: Compare 20 pairs of decimals (like 0.305 vs 0.35) by lining up place values and record with symbols.

days.title: Ordering game
days.work: Play 'Decimal Line-Up': draw 5 index cards with decimals and order them least to greatest on a number line, then order Olympic race times.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz writing decimals in three forms and comparing/ordering 10 sets, then explain one error a student might make.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on decimal forms and comparisons; observation of ordering game reasoning.

objectives: Round decimals to the nearest whole, tenth and hundredth
Use a number line to justify rounding

days.title: Rounding on a number line
days.work: Round 12 decimals to the nearest tenth by placing them on a vertical number line between two benchmarks and marking the midpoint.

days.title: Rounding to any place
days.work: Round the same 10 numbers (like 4.386) to the nearest whole, tenth and hundredth and compare results in a table.

days.title: Rounding in context
days.work: Round prices on a grocery receipt to the nearest dollar and estimate the total, then compare to the actual total.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed review of place value, powers of 10, comparing and rounding, and make a one-page 'decimal place value' reference sheet.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Take the Unit 1 test (place value, exponents, comparing, rounding) and complete a self-reflection on the hardest item.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 test covering 5.NBT.A.1–A.4.

objectives: Estimate products by rounding
Multiply multi-digit numbers using area models and the standard algorithm

days.title: Estimating products
days.work: Round factors to estimate 15 products (like 389 x 42 ≈ 400 x 40) and do a 3-minute multiplication fact fluency check.

days.title: Area model
days.work: Solve 8 problems such as 236 x 34 with an area model and add the partial products.

days.title: Standard algorithm 3x2
days.work: Connect partial products to the standard algorithm and solve 10 three-digit by two-digit problems on grid paper to keep columns aligned.

days.title: Standard algorithm 4x2 and 3x3
days.work: Solve 10 larger problems like 2,407 x 56, checking each against an estimate.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 10-problem multiplication quiz and an error analysis: find and fix the mistake in 3 worked examples.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on standard-algorithm multiplication with estimation checks.

weeks.topic: Numerical expressions and multiplication word problems
objectives: Evaluate expressions with parentheses, brackets and braces
Write and interpret expressions without evaluating

days.title: Grouping symbols
days.work: Evaluate 15 expressions with parentheses such as (6 + 4) x 3 vs 6 + 4 x 3 and discuss why the answers differ.

days.title: Brackets and braces
days.work: Evaluate nested expressions like 2 x {5 + [12 - (3 x 2)]}, working from the inside out on 12 problems.

days.title: Writing expressions
days.work: Translate 12 phrases like 'add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2' into expressions and write phrases for given expressions.

days.title: Interpreting expressions
days.work: Explain without calculating why 3 x (18,932 + 921) is three times as large as 18,932 + 921, then solve 5 multi-step multiplication word problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play 'Target 24' with dice to build expressions, then take a 12-item quiz on evaluating and writing expressions.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on evaluating and writing numerical expressions; word problem solutions with labeled answers.

objectives: Divide using area models and partial quotients
Use multiplication to check division

days.title: Division by multiples of 10
days.work: Use basic facts and place value to solve 15 problems like 2,400 / 60 and 420 / 30.

days.title: Area model division
days.work: Solve 8 problems such as 1,512 / 24 by building an area model with known parts of the dividend.

days.title: Partial quotients
days.work: Use partial quotients with friendly multiples (10x, 5x, 2x the divisor) to solve 8 four-digit by two-digit problems.

days.title: Checking with multiplication
days.work: Solve 6 division problems and check each with multiplication plus remainder; write how the check confirms the answer.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz of 8 division problems showing a model or partial quotients for each.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on division with two-digit divisors using models.

weeks.topic: Estimating quotients, interpreting remainders, unit assessment
objectives: Estimate quotients using compatible numbers
Interpret remainders in word problems

days.title: Compatible numbers
days.work: Estimate 15 quotients like 3,476 / 58 ≈ 3,600 / 60 and decide whether the actual quotient is greater or less.

days.title: Adjusting estimates
days.work: Divide 8 problems where the first estimate is too high or too low and adjust the trial quotient.

days.title: Interpreting remainders
days.work: Solve 8 word problems (buses for 230 students, packs of 24 pencils) and decide whether to round up, drop or use the remainder.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed review of multiplication, expressions and division and write your own word problem for each.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Take the Unit 2 test on multi-digit multiplication, division and numerical expressions.

weeks.assessment: Unit 2 test covering 5.NBT.B.5, 5.NBT.B.6, 5.OA.A.1–A.2.

objectives: Add and subtract decimals to hundredths using models and place value
Estimate decimal sums and differences

days.title: Modeling decimal addition
days.work: Shade hundredths grids to add 10 pairs like 0.46 + 0.38 and record with a place value equation.

days.title: Adding with regrouping
days.work: Add 15 decimals including different numbers of places (4.7 + 12.35) by lining up place values and using zero placeholders.

days.title: Subtracting decimals
days.work: Subtract 15 problems like 8 - 2.36 using models and then the written method, checking by adding.

days.title: Shopping problems
days.work: Use a store flyer to plan purchases under $50, adding prices and subtracting from the budget for 5 scenarios.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a 12-problem quiz on decimal addition and subtraction including 2 word problems.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on decimal addition and subtraction; budget scenarios checked for accuracy.

objectives: Multiply decimals by whole numbers
Multiply decimals by decimals using area models and place value reasoning

days.title: Decimal x whole number
days.work: Solve 12 problems like 4 x 0.36 using repeated addition, disks, and then multiplication, comparing the results.

days.title: Tenths x tenths
days.work: Shade overlapping areas on a hundredths grid to model 0.3 x 0.6 = 0.18 for 8 problems.

days.title: Placing the decimal point
days.work: Multiply 12 problems like 2.4 x 1.3 as whole numbers, then place the decimal by estimating and by counting place values.

days.title: Decimal products in context
days.work: Solve 6 word problems such as the cost of 3.5 pounds of apples at $1.29 per pound.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on 10 decimal multiplication problems and explain why 0.5 x 0.4 is smaller than both factors.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on decimal multiplication with written explanation.

objectives: Divide decimals by whole numbers
Divide by decimals using equivalent division problems

days.title: Decimal / whole number
days.work: Use disks to share 4.8 among 4 and solve 12 problems like 6.24 / 3 with the written method.

days.title: Decimal / whole number with zeros
days.work: Solve 10 problems like 7.5 / 6 where zeros must be annexed to the dividend to finish.

days.title: Dividing by tenths
days.work: Model 2 / 0.5 as 'how many halves in 2' and solve 10 problems like 3.6 / 0.4 using grids.

days.title: Equivalent division
days.work: Multiply dividend and divisor by 10 or 100 to rewrite 1.44 / 0.12 as 144 / 12 and solve 10 such problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on 10 decimal division problems and check two of them with multiplication.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on decimal division with multiplication checks.

weeks.topic: Decimal word problems and unit assessment
objectives: Choose the correct operation for decimal word problems
Solve multi-step decimal problems

days.title: Which operation?
days.work: Sort 12 decimal word problems by operation and solve 6 of them with a bar model.

days.title: Unit price
days.work: Compare unit prices for 4 pairs of grocery items (e.g., 12 oz for $3.48 vs 16 oz for $4.32) by dividing.

days.title: Recipe scaling
days.work: Multiply a recipe's decimal measurements by 2.5 and divide by 2 to make a double-and-a-half batch and a half batch.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed decimal operations review and a 'my mistakes' log of errors to watch.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Take the Unit 3 test on all four decimal operations and word problems.

weeks.assessment: Unit 3 test covering 5.NBT.B.7.

objectives: Generate equivalent fractions
Find common denominators for unlike fractions

days.title: Equivalent fractions review
days.work: Fold paper strips to show 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8 and generate 3 equivalent fractions for each of 10 fractions using multiplication.

days.title: Simplifying
days.work: Simplify 15 fractions by dividing by common factors and match simplified and unsimplified fraction cards.

days.title: Common denominators
days.work: List multiples to find common denominators for 12 pairs like 2/3 and 3/4 and rename both fractions.

days.title: Comparing unlike fractions
days.work: Compare 12 pairs of unlike fractions by renaming with common denominators and by benchmark reasoning.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on equivalent fractions, simplifying and common denominators.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on equivalent fractions and common denominators.

weeks.topic: Adding and subtracting fractions with unlike denominators
objectives: Add fractions with unlike denominators
Subtract fractions with unlike denominators

days.title: Adding with models
days.work: Use fraction strips to add 1/2 + 1/3 and 8 other pairs, recording the renamed equation for each.

days.title: Adding with equations
days.work: Add 15 pairs of unlike fractions by renaming, writing sums greater than 1 as mixed numbers.

days.title: Subtracting with models
days.work: Model 3/4 - 1/6 on a number line and solve 8 more subtraction problems with models.

days.title: Subtracting with equations
days.work: Subtract 15 unlike-fraction problems and simplify answers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a 12-problem quiz on adding and subtracting unlike fractions.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on adding/subtracting unlike fractions.

objectives: Add mixed numbers with unlike denominators
Subtract mixed numbers including regrouping

days.title: Mixed numbers and improper fractions
days.work: Convert 15 numbers between mixed and improper form using fraction circles and then multiplication.

days.title: Adding mixed numbers
days.work: Add 12 mixed numbers like 2 3/4 + 1 2/3, renaming and regrouping fraction sums greater than 1.

days.title: Subtracting mixed numbers
days.work: Subtract 12 mixed numbers like 5 1/4 - 2 2/3, regrouping a whole when needed.

days.title: Kitchen fractions
days.work: Use measuring cups to combine 1 1/2 cups and 2/3 cup of water, then compute the total and how much more is needed to make 3 cups.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on adding and subtracting mixed numbers.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on mixed number addition and subtraction.

objectives: Solve fraction addition and subtraction word problems
Use benchmark fractions to judge reasonableness

days.title: Benchmark estimation
days.work: Estimate 15 sums and differences by rounding fractions to 0, 1/2 or 1 on a number line.

days.title: Bar models for word problems
days.work: Solve 6 word problems with bar models, such as a hiker who walked 2 1/3 miles then 1 3/4 miles.

days.title: Spotting unreasonable answers
days.work: Judge 8 solutions (like 2/5 + 1/2 = 3/7) as reasonable or not using benchmarks and correct the wrong ones.

days.title: Write your own
days.work: Write and solve 4 fraction word problems about a garden or recipe, including one subtraction with regrouping.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a word problem quiz requiring a model, equation and estimate check for each problem.

weeks.assessment: Word-problem quiz scored on model, equation, answer and estimate.

weeks.topic: Line plots with fractional data and unit assessment
objectives: Make line plots of measurements in fractions of a unit
Solve problems using data from line plots

days.title: Collect data
days.work: Measure 12 pencils or leaves to the nearest 1/8 inch and record the data in a table.

days.title: Build the line plot
days.work: Draw a line plot of the measurement data with a scale in eighths and title and label it.

days.title: Questions from the plot
days.work: Use the line plot to find the total length, the difference between longest and shortest, and how much liquid each beaker would hold if redistributed equally.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed review of unlike fractions, mixed numbers and line plot problems.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Take the Unit 4 test on adding and subtracting fractions and line plots.

weeks.assessment: Unit 4 test covering 5.NF.A.1–A.2 and 5.MD.B.2; graded line plot.

objectives: Interpret a/b as a divided by b
Solve sharing problems with fractional answers

days.title: Sharing wholes
days.work: Cut paper circles to share 3 pizzas among 4 people and record 3 / 4 = 3/4; repeat for 4 other sharing situations.

days.title: Division as fraction
days.work: Write 15 division expressions as fractions and fractions as division (7 / 3 = 7/3 = 2 1/3).

days.title: Between which wholes?
days.work: Decide between which two whole numbers each of 10 quotients like 47 / 6 lies, and write each as a mixed number.

days.title: Word problems
days.work: Solve 6 sharing problems such as 50 pounds of rice shared among 8 families.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on fractions as division and explain one problem with a drawing.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on interpreting fractions as division.

weeks.topic: Multiplying a fraction and a whole number
objectives: Multiply a whole number by a fraction
Find a fraction of a set

days.title: Fraction of a set
days.work: Use 24 counters to find 1/3, 2/3, 3/4 and 5/6 of the set and write each as multiplication.

days.title: Tape diagrams
days.work: Draw tape diagrams to solve 10 problems like 3/5 x 40.

days.title: Whole x fraction
days.work: Solve 12 problems like 6 x 2/3 using repeated addition and then (6 x 2)/3.

days.title: Word problems
days.work: Solve 6 problems such as 'Maria read 3/4 of a 220-page book; how many pages did she read?'

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on fraction-by-whole-number multiplication.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on multiplying fractions and whole numbers.

weeks.topic: Multiplying fractions by fractions and area
objectives: Multiply fractions by fractions using area models
Find areas of rectangles with fractional side lengths

days.title: Folding paper
days.work: Fold paper to show 1/2 of 1/3 and 2/3 of 3/4 and record the product for 6 problems.

days.title: Area models
days.work: Shade overlapping regions to solve 10 fraction x fraction problems, then notice the numerator x numerator / denominator x denominator rule.

days.title: Fractional side lengths
days.work: Tile a 3/4 inch by 2/3 inch rectangle with unit fraction squares and compute areas of 8 rectangles by multiplying sides.

days.title: Mixed numbers
days.work: Multiply 8 mixed number problems like 2 1/2 x 1 1/3 using area models with partial products.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on multiplying fractions and finding areas with fractional sides.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on fraction multiplication and fractional area.

weeks.topic: Multiplication as scaling and real-world problems
objectives: Predict product size without multiplying
Solve real-world fraction multiplication problems

days.title: Scaling predictions
days.work: Without calculating, decide whether 15 products like 3/4 x 12 or 1 1/2 x 12 are greater than, less than or equal to 12, and justify.

days.title: Resizing pictures
days.work: Redraw a simple grid picture at 1/2 size and 1 1/2 size and explain how the scale factor changed it.

days.title: Real-world problems
days.work: Solve 6 problems such as scaling a recipe by 2/3 or finding 3/8 of a 2 1/2 mile trail.

days.title: Mixed practice
days.work: Complete 15 mixed fraction multiplication problems and simplify answers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz with scaling questions and multi-step fraction multiplication word problems.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on scaling and real-world fraction multiplication.

weeks.topic: Dividing unit fractions and whole numbers
objectives: Divide a unit fraction by a whole number
Divide a whole number by a unit fraction

days.title: Unit fraction / whole
days.work: Share 1/2 of a pan of brownies among 3 people with a drawing and solve 8 problems like 1/3 / 4.

days.title: Whole / unit fraction
days.work: Use number lines to find how many 1/4s are in 3 and solve 8 problems like 5 / 1/3.

days.title: Checking with multiplication
days.work: Check 10 division answers with multiplication (1/12 x 4 = 1/3) and explain the relationship.

days.title: Story contexts
days.work: Write story contexts for 1/4 / 2 and 6 / 1/2, then solve both with models.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on dividing unit fractions and whole numbers with models.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on unit fraction division.

weeks.topic: Fraction division word problems and unit assessment
objectives: Solve real-world problems with fraction division
Choose between fraction multiplication and division

days.title: Serving sizes
days.work: Use a 1/3 cup measure to find how many servings are in 2 cups of rice, then solve 5 similar problems.

days.title: Multiply or divide?
days.work: Sort 10 fraction word problems as multiplication or division and solve them with diagrams.

days.title: Multi-step problems
days.work: Solve 4 multi-step problems combining fraction multiplication, division and addition.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a cumulative review of fractions as division, multiplication, scaling and division.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Take the Unit 5 test on multiplying and dividing fractions.

weeks.assessment: Unit 5 test covering 5.NF.B.3–B.7.

objectives: Define volume as cubic units filling a solid
Measure volume by counting cubes

days.title: What is volume?
days.work: Fill 3 small boxes with sugar cubes and compare which holds the most; define a unit cube and cubic unit.

days.title: Building prisms
days.work: Build 6 rectangular prisms with given dimensions from cubes and record the number of cubes in each.

days.title: Layers
days.work: Count cubes in one layer and multiply by number of layers for 8 prism pictures.

days.title: Nets and boxes
days.work: Cut out and fold box nets, predict how many centimeter cubes fill each, then test.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz finding volume of prisms by counting cubes and layers.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on volume by counting unit cubes; observation during building.

objectives: Apply V = l x w x h
Apply V = B x h

days.title: V = l x w x h
days.work: Connect layers of cubes to the formula and find volumes of 12 prisms with given dimensions.

days.title: V = B x h
days.work: Find the base area and multiply by height for 10 prisms; show the associative property gives the same volume.

days.title: Measuring real boxes
days.work: Measure 4 household boxes to the nearest inch and calculate their volumes in cubic inches.

days.title: Missing dimensions
days.work: Solve 8 problems where volume and two dimensions are known and find the third.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on volume formulas and missing dimensions.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on V = lwh and V = Bh; box measurement table.

weeks.topic: Composite figures and volume design project
objectives: Find volumes of figures composed of two rectangular prisms
Design a box to meet volume requirements

days.title: Composite figures
days.work: Decompose 8 L-shaped and step-shaped figures into two prisms and add their volumes.

days.title: Real-world composite volume
days.work: Find the volume of a two-level planter box and a staircase made of blocks.

days.title: Design challenge
days.work: Design 3 different boxes with a volume of exactly 72 cubic inches and choose the one using the least cardboard.

days.title: Build and present
days.work: Build the chosen box from cardstock and present its dimensions, volume calculation and design reasoning.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Take the Unit 6 test on volume concepts, formulas and composite figures.

weeks.assessment: Unit 6 test and box design project rubric.

objectives: Convert length, weight and capacity in customary units
Solve conversion word problems

days.title: Length conversions
days.work: Measure the room in feet and convert to inches and yards; complete 15 length conversion problems.

days.title: Weight conversions
days.work: Weigh items on a kitchen scale in ounces and convert to pounds; solve 12 problems including fractional pounds.

days.title: Capacity conversions
days.work: Fill a gallon jug using cups, pints and quarts and create a conversion chart; solve 12 capacity problems.

days.title: Mixed units
days.work: Convert and compute with mixed units like 5 ft 8 in - 3 ft 10 in and 2 lb 6 oz x 3.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on customary conversions with 5 word problems.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on customary unit conversions.

weeks.topic: Metric conversions and multi-step measurement problems
objectives: Convert metric units using powers of 10
Solve multi-step conversion problems

days.title: Metric length
days.work: Measure objects in mm, cm and m and convert 15 measurements by multiplying or dividing by 10, 100 and 1,000.

days.title: Metric mass and capacity
days.work: Measure liquids in mL and L and masses in g and kg; solve 12 conversion problems.

days.title: Multi-step problems
days.work: Solve 6 multi-step problems such as how many 250 mL cups can be filled from three 2 L bottles.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed customary and metric review and make a conversion reference card.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Take the Unit 7 test on converting measurement units.

weeks.assessment: Unit 7 test covering 5.MD.A.1.

objectives: Identify axes, origin and ordered pairs
Plot and name points in the first quadrant

days.title: Building the plane
days.work: Tape a floor grid with x- and y-axes and walk to ordered pairs called out, noting that x comes first.

days.title: Plotting points
days.work: Plot 20 points on graph paper and name the coordinates of 10 given points.

days.title: Coordinate pictures
days.work: Plot and connect a list of ordered pairs to reveal a mystery picture, then design your own for someone else.

days.title: Distances on lines
days.work: Find the distance between points that share an x- or y-coordinate on 10 problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play coordinate 'Battleship' and take a quiz on plotting and naming points.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on coordinate plane vocabulary and plotting.

objectives: Represent real-world situations as points on a graph
Interpret coordinates in context

days.title: Graphing data
days.work: Record outdoor temperature every hour for 6 hours and graph (hour, temperature) points.

days.title: Choosing scales
days.work: Graph 3 data sets (savings over weeks, plant height over days) choosing appropriate axis scales.

days.title: Interpreting graphs
days.work: Answer 10 questions about what specific points mean on a graph of a bike trip's time and distance.

days.title: Map coordinates
days.work: Draw a neighborhood map on a coordinate grid and write directions between locations using coordinates.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz graphing and interpreting a real-world data set.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on graphing and interpreting real-world points.

objectives: Generate two patterns from rules
Graph ordered pairs from corresponding terms and describe relationships

days.title: Two rules
days.work: Generate patterns 'add 3' and 'add 6' starting at 0 in a table and describe how corresponding terms compare.

days.title: Graphing patterns
days.work: Form ordered pairs from 4 pairs of patterns and graph them, noting the straight-line pattern.

days.title: Real-world patterns
days.work: Create tables for 'cost of tickets at $4' vs '$8' and graph to compare.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed review of coordinate plane, graphing and patterns.

days.title: Unit 8 test
days.work: Take the Unit 8 test on coordinate graphing and numerical patterns.

weeks.assessment: Unit 8 test covering 5.G.A.1–A.2 and 5.OA.B.3.

objectives: Identify attributes of polygons
Classify triangles by sides and angles

days.title: Polygon attributes
days.work: Sort 20 shape cut-outs by number of sides, parallel sides and right angles, recording attributes in a table.

days.title: Classifying triangles
days.work: Measure sides and angles of 12 triangles and classify each by sides and by angles.

days.title: Can it exist?
days.work: Try to draw 8 triangles (e.g., right obtuse, equilateral right) and explain which are impossible.

days.title: Attribute riddles
days.work: Write 5 'Who am I?' shape riddles using precise geometric attributes and solve a partner's riddles.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on polygon attributes and triangle classification.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on attributes and classifying triangles.

objectives: Classify quadrilaterals in a hierarchy
Explain why a figure belongs to multiple categories
materials: geoboard or Math Learning Center Geoboard app

days.title: Quadrilateral family
days.work: Build each quadrilateral type on a geoboard and list its defining properties.

days.title: Hierarchy diagram
days.work: Create a hierarchy diagram from quadrilateral down to square with arrows and property labels.

days.title: Always, sometimes, never
days.work: Decide whether 12 statements like 'a rhombus is a square' are always, sometimes or never true, with drawings as proof.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a review of triangle and quadrilateral classification using a Venn diagram.

days.title: Unit 9 test
days.work: Take the Unit 9 test on classifying two-dimensional figures.

weeks.assessment: Unit 9 test covering 5.G.B.3–B.4; hierarchy diagram.

weeks.topic: Cumulative review: whole numbers, decimals and expressions
objectives: Maintain fluency with multi-digit multiplication and division
Solve multi-step decimal problems

days.title: Multiplication fluency
days.work: Complete a timed set of 10 multi-digit multiplication problems and track accuracy.

days.title: Division review
days.work: Solve 8 division problems with two-digit divisors and interpret remainders in 3 word problems.

days.title: Decimal operations
days.work: Complete a 20-problem decimal operation scavenger hunt with task cards around the house.

days.title: Expressions and conversions
days.work: Evaluate 8 expressions with grouping symbols and solve 5 measurement conversion problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a cumulative quiz on number and operations in base ten.

weeks.assessment: Cumulative quiz on NBT, OA and conversions.

weeks.topic: Cumulative review: fractions, volume and geometry
objectives: Perform all fraction operations accurately
Apply volume and coordinate graphing skills

days.title: Fraction add/subtract
days.work: Solve 12 mixed number addition and subtraction problems and 2 word problems.

days.title: Fraction multiply/divide
days.work: Solve 12 fraction multiplication and unit-fraction division problems and explain 1 with a model.

days.title: Volume and geometry
days.work: Find volumes of 6 prisms and composite figures and classify 6 quadrilaterals.

days.title: Graphing
days.work: Graph and interpret a pattern table and a real-world data set on a coordinate plane.

days.title: End-of-year assessment
days.work: Take the end-of-year cumulative assessment covering all fifth-grade domains.

weeks.assessment: End-of-year cumulative assessment.

objectives: Apply fractions, decimals, volume and graphing to a real project
Communicate mathematical reasoning in a presentation
materials: garden store flyer or website prices

days.title: Design the layout
days.work: Draw a garden plan on a coordinate grid, labeling the corners of each bed with ordered pairs.

days.title: Planter volume
days.work: Calculate the soil volume for 2 raised planter boxes (including one composite shape) and convert to cubic feet.

days.title: Fractions of space
days.work: Decide what fraction of each bed gets each plant and compute the area for each crop with fraction multiplication.

days.title: Budget
days.work: Use decimal prices to total seeds, soil and boards, staying under a $150 budget.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the garden plan to family, explaining each calculation, and complete a year-end math reflection.

weeks.assessment: Capstone project rubric: accuracy of calculations, use of grid and units, clarity of explanation.
